newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-ARGENTINA INVOLVED IN MORE MAYHEM IN BOLIVIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA INVOLVED IN MORE MAYHEM IN BOLIVIA.

text.p: Argentina, who had two players sent off and were involved in a massive brawl on their last visit to Bolivia less than three months ago, were protagonists in another shambolic match as they bowed out of the Copa America Saturday.
The Argentines had three players sent off as they suffered a shock 2-1 quarter-final defeat to Peru after once again losing their heads and getting into a fight when the chips were down.
Under coach Daniel Passarella, Argentina appear to have become incapable of accepting a defeat without getting into trouble.
Their previous defeat had been in April's World Cup qualifier in La Paz when they lost 2-1 to Bolivia.

On that occasion, two Argentines were sent off, goalkeeper Ignacio Gonzalez head-butted an opponent in an incident missed by match officials and the entire team became involved in a brawl with members of the Bolivian bench. The fight, which needed police intervention, held up play for ten minutes near the end of the game.

Julio Grondona, president of the Argentina Football Federation, was subsequently questioned over the incident by the Argentina's Congress, worried about the damage caused to a nation bidding to host the 2004 Olymic Games.

FIFA, soccer's governing body, handed out suspensions to Gonzalez and the two players sent off, fined coach Daniel Passarella but took no other action. These punishments were clearly not strong enough to deter Argentina from a repeat performance, as Saturday's incidents showed.
The fight that resulted in two red cards began in the 72nd minute because Peru goalkeeper Miguel Miranda did not want to give Argentina the ball back.
Argentina, trailing 2-0, had been awarded a penalty which was converted by Marcelo Gallardo.

Gallardo then rushed to the net to retrieve the ball and get the game re-started quickly but Miranda got to it at the same time. The two began pushing, other players joined in and a brawl ensued that held up play for three minutes and ended with Gallardo and Eduardo Berizzo being shown the red card.
Shortly afterwards, Zapata, one of the players dismissed in La Paz in April, was sent off for a second bookable offence.
The game ended a miserable tournament for Argentina.

Passarella had been unhappy even before he arrived, claiming his team already had enough to worry about with a marathon World Cup qualifying competition that forces them to play 16 times in 18 months. His answer was to bring a second-string team.

Having fought their way through the first round without ever looking convincing, Argentina were then victims of a sudden change in the rules which would have condemned them to a quarter-final in high altitude La Paz if Bolivia had been their opponents.
A furious Passarella threatened to take his team home but the crisis was averted when Bolivia, who would have played Argentina if they finished second in their first round group, came top.
All this was topped with Saturday's fiasco when the team were outplayed for long periods by Peru.
Eddie Carrazas fired Peru in front after half an hour when the ball was passed to him by an Argentina player and Martin Hidalgo finished off a delightful move with a low drive in the 62nd minute.

In between, goalkeeper Miranda had stopped everything Argentina could throw at him, including a penalty by Gallardo who remarkably repeated Tuesday's performance against Paraguay when he missed one penalty and scored from another.

"We were eliminated by our own failings, that is the truth," said Passarella. "When I took over I said the priority was to qualify for the World Cup, which we are doing. To not qualify for the World Cup would be a failure, a bad World Cup would be a failure."

Passarella then bemused reporters with the comment: "This Argentina national team is the Argentina national team. Today and yesterday, it was the Argentina national team, all of these players are top level."
Peru were left to contemplate a semi-final against the winners of Sunday's Brazil-Paraguay match.
They were joined in the semi-finals by hosts Bolivia who, once again using the advantage of playing in La Paz at 3,600 metres above sea level, beat Colombia 2-1.
Colombia had played Brazil at sea level in the first round less than 48 hours earlier and arrived in La Paz only two hours before the start to try and reduce the effects of altitude.

But they fell behind in less time than it takes to say the words oxygen mask, Marco Etcheverry scoring from a free kick after three minutes. Erwin Sanchez increased the lead 20 minutes later with a shot that bounced under the arms of goalkeeper Farid Mondragon.

Herman Gaviria pulled a second half goal back for Colombia, but they never seemed to have the lungs to force an equaliser. The highlight was provided by Bolivia's Julio Cesar Baldivieso, who hit the crossbar from near the halfway line after seeing Mondragon off his line.
